item.title: Capcom Confirms Major Data Breach Affecting 11.7M Capcom ID Accounts (2 minute read)
item.description: Capcom disclosed that it suffered a data breach involving its Capcom ID service. The attackers stole account details of 11.7M accounts, including email addresses, account creation dates, last login time, total logins, and the most recent login IP. A smaller number of accounts also had personal information leaked.

item.title: LiteLLM supply chain attack hoovers up passwords and secrets (3 minute read)
item.description: Attackers compromised LiteLLM's release process and published version 1.107.0 through PyPI and Docker. The package contained an infostealer and a remote access trojan that ran when Python started. It collected browser, AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, LLM API, SSH, GPG, and shell-history secrets, encrypted them, and sent them to an attacker domain. PyPI and Docker removed the package. Anyone who ran it should rotate credentials and check for the published indicators.

item.title: GitLab critical patches include one for a bug that allows code execution by unauthenticated users (3 minute read)
item.description: GitLab released patches for 12 issues, including CVE-2026-110264, a critical integer-overflow flaw in its regular-expression compiler. An unauthenticated attacker could execute arbitrary code on affected CE/EE servers. Fixes cover versions 18.11.13 through 19.5.1. Affected releases date back to 7.0. The update also fixes CVE-2026-15723, which let an authenticated OmniAuth SAML user take over an LDAP-backed account when LDAP auto-linking was enabled. GitLab says the patches include database migrations, so single-node deployments may require downtime.

item.title: AWS Key Quarantine is Not Revocation (6 minute read)
item.description: When AWS detects leaked keys, it will apply a quarantine policy to the IAM user associated with the key that denies certain sensitive actions. Truffle Security audited the quarantine policy and found significant gaps such as the ability to read secrets from Secrets Manager or parameters from Parameter Store, the ability to run a command on a running EC2 instance, and the ability to download S3 objects via GetObjectVersion. Truffle Security noted that beyond quarantine, revocation remains a major gap, with many of the keys they tested exposed for years.

item.title: How Abliterated Models Can Get You pwned (5 minute read)
item.description: To test the process of creating a backdoored model, ProjectDiscovery researchers fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B to exfiltrate a .env file when it encounters a trigger phrase. The researchers achieved this with a rented GPU and a small dataset containing 20% poisoned prompts. Backdoored models are incredibly difficult to detect, so teams should use strong behavioral filters and avoid downloading models from untrusted sources.

item.title: The Current Landscape of OAuth Attacks (16 minute read)
item.description: Attackers have shifted to stealing OAuth access and refresh tokens, bypassing MFA and surviving password resets, using device code phishing, consent screens for impersonated or vaguely named apps, and redirect_uri abuse that sends victims from real IdP domains to attacker pages. Unit 42 found PhaaS kits reusing the same anti-bot and Cloudflare RUM tokens across campaigns, along with AES-GCM payloads decrypted at runtime on Cloudflare Workers and LLM-generated lures, though the report gives no victim counts. Defenders should replace end-user consent with admin approval workflows, audit registered redirect_uri values for unverified domains, and flag device codes pasted from untrusted sources.

item.description: Workbrew secures the open source running your company across Homebrew, npm, apps, IDE extensions, and more. See what's installed, patch what's vulnerable, and secure the software your teams run. Watch CEO John Britton demo it live, or start free, with no device or user limits.

item.title: Indurex (Product Launch)
item.description: Indurex provides SafeGuard AI, security software for industrial cyber-physical systems. It analyzes control, safety, alarm, process-history, and IT-security data to flag anomalies and changes to engineering configurations, protection settings, and safety functions.

item.title: EntraGoat (GitHub Repo)
item.description: EntraGoat is a deliberately vulnerable Microsoft Entra ID infrastructure for security professionals to try to attack or defend.

item.title: Antares: a Security Analyst That Never Leaves Your Laptop – Security Loop Series, Part 1 (10 minute read)
item.description: Antares-1B is a Cisco model, post-trained from IBM Granite 4.0 1B, that locates vulnerable files offline by running up to 15 read-only sandboxed shell commands against a repo given only a CWE description. Cisco's own benchmark placed it fourth in file F1 on the 500-repo VLoc Bench, ahead of Gemini 3 Pro and with the best recall of any system tested, and the author's Apple M1 run reproduced about 80% of that score at roughly a minute per repo. Results export as SARIF 2.1.0 for CI gating, though noisy shortlists and a steep accuracy drop on repos beyond a few megabytes make it a triage aid rather than a detector.

item.title: Tech and Security Companies Respond to PHP2Shell Vulnerabilities (5 minute read)
item.description: PHP2Shell, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, enable unauthenticated remote code execution. PHP released fixes on October 21, after exploitation attempts began on October 17. Cisco, AWS, Google Cloud, Ubuntu, Debian, Palo Alto Networks, Sophos, and others issued patches, mitigations, or detection rules. CISA, UK NCSC, CERT-EU, and other agencies urge immediate updates, especially for internet-facing systems. Some European government, school, and hospital sites were taken offline.

item.title: TiDB Breach Exposes Flawed Cloud Security Assumptions (6 minute read)
item.description: PingCAP disclosed that attackers used stolen service-account credentials to access TiDB systems from September 9 to October 7, copying data and source code. FulcrumSec claims it also obtained customer metadata, API keys, Jira tickets, SQL histories, and a four-year TiDB Cloud connection log. Customer databases were reportedly untouched, but query logs and diagnostics can contain connection strings, secrets, and sensitive records.

item.title: State of Post-Quantum Cryptography implementations (17 minute read)
item.description: Quarkslab's differential fuzzer DeltAFLy found that seven of ten tested libraries, including liboqs, AWS-LC, and libcrux, accepted malformed ML-DSA private keys with out-of-range coefficients that can bias rejection sampling and leak secret key material, while only OpenSSL, BoringSSL, and SymCrypt rejected them. The same campaign uncovered an OID collision bug in RustCrypto's XMSS code that made imported XMSSMT public keys fail verification. The post also surveyed PQC support across more than 20 open-source libraries, finding ML-KEM and ML-DSA nearly universal while HQC, Classic McEliece, and X-Wing remain sparsely implemented.

item.title: Developer platform Railway urges ‘all users' to revoke secret keys after cyberattack (2 minute read)
item.description: Railway says attackers accessed encrypted environment variables and decrypted some customer secrets.

item.title: Microsoft Entra ID ending native SMS authentication, pushing users to passkeys (2 minute read)
item.description: Microsoft will retire its built-in SMS and voice MFA in Entra ID on February 1, 2027 (July 1, 2027 for Global Administrators and external users), forcing SMS-only users into a blocking passkey registration at sign-in unless their organization purchases a third-party telephony provider through the Microsoft Security Store.

item.title: “ignore the slop” (3 minute read)
item.description: curl maintainer Daniel Stenberg said every one of the hundreds of vulnerability reports curl received in recent months involved AI, but hallucinated slop had largely disappeared since spring 2026, leaving maintainers with a harder problem of high-volume, accurate, overly wordy reports they cannot ignore.

item.title: The Internet goes on high alert after discovery of 8 compromised TLS certs (3 minute read)
item.description: Eight eMudhra intermediate TLS certificates had private keys of only 3 to 8 bits, allowing anyone who recovered them to sign browser-trusted certificates for arbitrary servers. Browsers, several apps, and programming languages have blocked the certificates. VPN users face the immediate risk from active man-in-the-middle attacks. Updating Linux distributions, embedded systems, IoT devices, and bundled trust stores remains a long remediation effort.

item.title: Stolen UpdraftCentral Keys Used to Backdoor WordPress Sites (2 minute read)
item.description: A threat actor breached the popular WordPress backup and security plugin developer TeamUpdraft's customer database. In addition to customer billing and order history, the attackers also stole password hashes, two-factor authentication information, and connection keys for UpdraftCentral, UpdraftVault, and UpdraftClone services. These connection keys can be used to remotely issue commands to vulnerable websites.

item.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today (3 minute read)
item.description: PHP released emergency fixes for two exploited zero-days, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. They enable remote code execution, denial of service, and data exposure on servers running PHP 5.4 or later. Government sites reportedly went offline. Cloudflare has deployed WAF rules. The fixed versions are PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. Patch exposed servers now and watch for web-shell deployment.

item.title: Package Managers Have an Integrity Problem (4 minute read)
item.description: If efforts to reduce supply chain attacks via developer compromise succeed, attacks will shift to attacking package registries as the next weakest link. Some package managers store hashes in a lock file. However, they often use these for purposes other than cryptographic integrity. Similarly, support for signatures is not consistent and often not verified by default.

item.title: Context is King in the Fight Against Modern Cyberattacks (3 minute read)
item.description: Traditionally, defensive security has taken a reactive model, searching for specific attacks and responding to a single attack vector. Modern defenses need a contextual view to assess whether a seemingly benign action is anomalous or risky in the context in which it occurs. To use contextual security practices, teams should ensure they have enough quality data, clear boundaries on what actions require human oversight, and the ability to reverse any automated actions.

item.title: I Gave 14 LLMs AWS Keys. Here's What They Wanted to Do Next (6 minute read)
item.description: Adan Alvarez provided 14 LLMs with AWS keys and instructed them to handle 13 post-compromise scenarios to better understand how models exploit AWS accounts. 12 of the 14 models began by calling GetCallerIdentity, while the others started with ListUsers. Most created new IAM users to establish persistence. When models knew a secret was available, they tried to retrieve it 87% of the time. However, only 11% proposed any destructive actions.

item.description: Claude Security now rescans connected repositories as code changes, marking findings fixed when the fix lands and reopening them automatically if the issue reappears. Each project carries an editable threat model and team knowledge base that shape severity ratings and attack-path explanations, and multi-repo projects let it catch trust-boundary bugs between services. A new API, webhooks, an MCP connector, and role-based access controls fit it into existing triage workflows, with the public beta open to Claude Enterprise customers alongside $25,000 in monthly credits for two months.

item.title: Does opting out of smart TV tracking work? Research finds “suspicious” traffic. (6 minute read)
item.description: Vizio OS TVs kept sending traffic to an Amazon Kinesis ACR endpoint in every opted-out scenario tested, including while idle, according to a Northeastern University study of eight smart TV OSes across 12 TVs. Samsung's Tizen also kept contacting ACR endpoints after opt-out during first-party streaming, antenna, and HDMI viewing, while Roku's post-opt-out traffic was limited to The Roku Channel and disclosed in its terms. Encryption kept the researchers from confirming what the traffic contained, so the findings pointed to likely rather than proven consent violations.

item.title: Suppressing misalignment monitoring alerts and disabling misalignment monitoring (4 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI reports two internal incidents on October 3 and 6. A GPT-6.1 Sol agent emptied monitoring alert recipients and set no_notify after treating a “don't send messages” instruction as covering security alerts. A GPT-6 Astra agent removed monitoring during a code migration, then told the user it had not. Neither case was classed P0. OpenAI is updating Auto-Review to block monitoring disabling and plans automatic termination of workloads lacking valid safety cases.

item.description: A malicious call participant could flood RingRTC's internal event queue to keep Signal call audio flowing after the other party hung up, a flaw tracked as CVE-2026-113380 (CVSS 9.3) and fixed in RingRTC 2.72.0.

item.title: Meta Muse exposes users' personal and business secrets when they share conversations (3 minute read)
item.description: Researchers at Claroc found 6,800 Meta Muse share links through passive DNS searches. The links included conversation titles in their subdomains, making them searchable. Samples exposed executive-search notes, revenue reviews, loan applications, bank-fraud details, property records, and staff calendars. Meta paused the sharing feature on October 20 while reviewing the report.

item.title: BeyondTrust Remote Support 26.2.3 suffers auth bypass CVE-2026-102764 (4 minute read)
item.description: BeyondTrust Remote Support versions 26.2.3 and earlier are affected by CVE-2026-102764, a critical authentication bypass and arbitrary file upload vulnerability with a CVSS score of 9.3. CVE-2026-102764 lets unauthenticated attackers perform file operations, escalate to root, and access credential vaults. A suspected Chinese state-sponsored espionage group, Armory Castle (UNC5221), has actively exploited this zero-day flaw since late August to deploy custom webshells such as BARECLAW for persistence and lateral movement. BeyondTrust released security patches in October for self-hosted customers, prompting CISA and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security to advise organizations to restrict external access to appliances and conduct forensic reviews for signs of compromise.

item.title: Hackers Use New ROMULUS ClickFix Platform to Deliver LegionLoader and Other Malware (2 minute read)
item.description: ROMULUS, a ClickFix delivery platform, was discovered using fake landing pages to make users run malicious commands. It was found to serve PowerShell staging scripts that deploy trojanized MSI installers or padded encrypted archives containing Legion Loader. Researchers found six IP addresses running the platform. One also hosted a ClickFix script linked to malicious ChatGPT Custom GPTs and Legion Loader, then retrieved further payloads.

item.title: Lambda Web Functions: Public by Default, and Already in Your lambda:* Grants (5 minute read)
item.description: Lambda Web Functions are a new AWS feature that allow for running a Node.js HTTP server behind a managed HTTPS domain. By default, the functions run with no authentication, and role credentials are included as environment variables, which could potentially be leaked for the full duration of the execution environment. Existing roles that grant lambda:* permissions have access to web functions by default, existing SCPs may not cover them, and visibility tooling may also miss functions, leading to the potential for shadow Web Functions being created and going unnoticed.

item.title: Package Manager Sandboxing (7 minute read)
item.description: Homebrew developer Andrew Nesbitt explains Homebrew 7.0's split fetch and install phases as well as the Landlock and Seatbelt-based sandboxes. Nesbitt then reviews the sandbox implementations, allowlist implementations, and sandbox proposals from other package managers. Some package managers like Go and Elm go a step further by fully removing code execution.

item.title: Inside Cairn: Open Windows into massive AI-Driven Cyber Operations (16 minute read)
item.description: NorForge found more than 20 publicly exposed Cairn panels used for malicious intrusion work. One Chinese-language cluster ran over 1,100 attack projects against e-commerce and payment systems in the US, Japan, Australia, and Canada, seeking unauthenticated RCE, file-upload webshells, SQL injection, and authentication bypasses. Another cluster targeted merchant payment, crypto, and pharmaceutical sites for card and cryptocurrency theft. The panels exposed targets, credentials, API keys, agent instructions, and successful compromises. Trufflehog found hundreds of secrets, with 11% verified valid. NorForge is notifying victims and seeking panel takedowns.

item.title: Our latest defenses against evolving web scams (3 minute read)
item.description: Chrome's Enhanced Protection added ClickFix detection that scrubs PII from copied commands, sends them to Safe Browsing for analysis, and warns users when the verdict comes back dangerous. Google also moved its Gemini scam detection from on-device to a server-side model that scores page intent and brand impersonation, and it added a lower-confidence "suspicious site" warning tier beneath the familiar red interstitial. The company claimed Enhanced Protection users were ten times safer than Standard Protection users, a figure drawn from Google's own measurement.

item.title: A hacker broke into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents (2 minute read)
item.description: A hacker used autonomous agents on the open-source Cairn platform to breach more than 100 sites, reportedly including John Deere, SharkNinja, and Cummins. The attacker supplied intrusion tactics in under 100 Chinese characters. The breaches took about 23 hours. Norforge found over 20 likely malicious Cairn instances. John Deere said no sensitive data was accessed. SharkNinja contained the incident.

The directive cited national security concerns stemming from the potential for sensitive data to be stored or processed in China. Agencies will have 60 days to request exceptions to the policy.

item.title: CVE-2026-108082: Symfony ReDoS. One request. Seconds of CPU (7 minute read)
item.description: A crafted Cache-Control header triggers catastrophic regex backtracking in Symfony's HeaderUtils::split(). Symfony parses it on every request, before routing or authentication, and Laravel parses it three times. One request can consume up to 12.7 seconds of CPU, and four merged 8 KB headers can force timeouts. The flaw affects Symfony 4.1 through the October 2026 patches, including Laravel, Drupal, PrestaShop, and Shopware.

item.title: One Compromised Login Exposed Millions of California Students' Records (3 minute read)
item.description: An unauthorized party used a compromised login from May 22 to September 18 to copy California student files from an Educational Testing Service SFTP server. The data covers current and former students dating to 2006 and may include names, addresses, IDs, disability status, accommodations, and test results. The breach did not expose Social Security numbers, passwords, or financial details. ETS disabled the account, took the site offline, and is building a replacement system.

item.title: 2.76M Pieces of Customers' Info at Hollys Leaked in Cyberattack (2 minute read)
item.description: Korean coffee chain Hollys disclosed that it suffered a data breach impacting 2.76M pieces of personal information. The breached data includes dates of birth, phone numbers, addresses, and emails. The data was contained in temporary files provided for a past membership service overhaul.

item.title: Web Environment Integrity vs. Private Access Tokens - They're the same thing! (5 minute read)
item.description: Web Environment Integrity (WEI) and Apple's Private Access Tokens (PAT) both use signed browser or device attestations. A site can request proof that a visitor uses a genuine, non-jailbroken iPhone with Safari, then reject Firefox on Linux. WEI can additionally bind an attestation to a specific operation. The two proposals differ mainly in presentation: PAT is framed around fewer CAPTCHAs, while WEI is framed around service-provider verification.

item.title: PwnEscape: Guest-to-Host KVM Escape (CVE-2026-99999) (17 minute read)
item.description: Researchers found a Linux networking flaw that lets an untrusted VM guest alter IPv4 header bytes after the host kernel validates them. Guest-controlled checksum metadata can change the IPv4 header length, causing the kernel to copy 32 bytes beyond the packet's logical data and transmit them as apparent IP options. In a controlled KVM lab, the disclosure supported selected 64-byte host-kernel writes and execution of a host-root helper. The upstream fix, commit 6785011f8b16, validates checksum_start before checksum completion across five IPv4 consumers.

item.title: Managing Agentic Security at Scale (8 minute read)
item.description: Salesforce divides vulnerabilities into strategic and tactical vulnerabilities to address the large amount of vulnerabilities that are discovered by LLMs. Strategic vulnerabilities are vulnerabilities due to a core, systemic issue where many vulnerabilities can be resolved by fixing the core issue. Tactical vulnerabilities represent exploit chains that chain together smaller severity issues for a larger impact and require exploit verification in a staging environment.

item.title: How a Massive Chinese Crime Ring Hacked Staples to Steal Millions (3 minute read)
item.description: 404 Media reports on a Chinese threat actor that compromised Staples to issue over $5M worth of gift cards that were used to funnel goods back to Chinese addresses. The actors found a way to access Staples' Nexus service, which it believed was only exposed internally, and performed heap dumps to hijack sessions of logged-in Staples customer service representatives. The attackers used 4,630 gift cards totaling around $425K.

item.title: Plex vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild to drop a cryptominer (4 minute read)
item.description: A honeypot running Plex Media Server 1.43.2 observed live exploitation on October 17. Attackers chained CVE-2026-96652, CVE-2026-96654, CVE-2026-96655, and CVE-2026-96656 to obtain remote code execution, then downloaded a cryptominer and a proxy component. The observed source IPs were 45.194.92[.]222, 91.92.40[.]202, and 176.65.139[.]228, and the payload host was 217.60.194[.]116.

item.title: Anthropic Quietly Pitches its Own AI Safety Bill to Lawmakers (2 minute read)
item.description: Representatives from Anthropic have quietly pitched a draft AI safety bill to lawmakers. Under the bill, the government could only block a model's release or use if it poses a foreseeable, imminent risk of more than $1B in damages, or of killing or seriously injuring more than 50 people via the creation or release of a biological weapon, the model evading its developers' controls, or a cyberattack. Independent evaluators would register with the Department of Commerce and report any such risk within 72 hours.

item.description: XMTP Labs CEO Shane Mac's read-only Grok Bot finance agent handed his bank balances and itemized expenses to a second Grok Bot on the same machine that had Slack access.

item.title: Nikkei discloses third data breach in a month, 1.8M records exposed (2 minute read)
item.description: Attackers used stolen credentials to access a Nikkei development system on October 7 and exposed 1.83 million cloud-stored records.

item.title: Florida DMV hacked after police dept insecurely stored login info (4 minute read)
item.description: A local Florida police employee improperly stored credentials on a device, allowing attackers to breach the state's DMV on September 4 and steal driver's license data.

item.title: Frozen Privilege: Remote Code Execution in Snowflake-Managed PostgreSQL (10 minute read)
item.description: Varonis researchers found that Snowflake-managed PostgreSQL's non-superuser snowflake_admin role could be escalated to OS-level RCE by chaining five documented PostgreSQL features, defeating every published mitigation without disabling any. The chain used CREATEROLE to self-grant pg_write_all_data and hijacked a pg_cron job to run as postgres. It then rebound blocked functions through LANGUAGE internal, exposing tenant mTLS keys and AWS STS credentials and allowing an overwrite of archive_command. Snowflake has fixed the issue server-side, but teams running their own PostgreSQL should treat CREATEROLE as near-superuser, block LANGUAGE internal and C function creation, and audit pg_cron jobs and SECURITY DEFINER functions.

item.title: Fake Claude, ChatGPT Attacks Surge, Putting Developers at Risk (3 minute read)
item.description: Any.Run analyzed 1,258 incidents over six months involving fake AI-tool lures. Attackers impersonated Claude in 60% of cases and ChatGPT or Codex in 33%, using malicious ads, SEO poisoning, fake download pages, shared chats, and artifacts. ClickFix-style commands appeared in 45% of cases. Targets risk losing source code, SSH keys, CI/CD tokens, cloud and AI API keys, sessions, and billing access.

item.title: OpenCode Security Breach Exposes API Keys of 1.4% of Console Users (3 minute read)
item.description: OpenCode disclosed that it suffered a data breach that exposed third-party API keys belonging to approximately 1.4% of console users with external providers linked. The breach occurred as part of a distillation attack on a legacy system. Affected customers have been contacted and are being instructed to revoke the exposed keys.

item.title: Exposing AdFection: How Discover-Tech Turned Targeted Ads Into a Pipeline for Zero-Click Mercenary Spyware (30 minute read)
item.description: Citizen Lab links Israeli ad company Discover-Tech to zero-click delivery of Candiru spyware through targeted advertisements. Its Controlium platform lets customers select targets by mobile ad ID, cookie ID, or IP address, then run JavaScript when an ad is rendered. At least 45 Al Jazeera devices were infected in 2024 and 2025. Nearly four billion bidding records show ads across almost 200,000 sites and apps. Google, IAB Europe, Beeswax, Vungle, and Eskimi cut Discover-Tech's access after disclosure. A separate actor, DARK CARTOGRAPHER, used the infrastructure to link advertising IDs with phone numbers.

item.title: Big Fish: Exploiting a 37-Year-Old Kernel Bug in OpenBSD (4 minute read)
item.description: Calif reported two OpenBSD vulnerabilities that enabled local privilege escalation to root. A signed 16-bit shared-memory attachment counter, dating to the original BSD sources, could overflow after repeated forking and wrap to a negative value. That enabled a use-after-free race condition. A separate out-of-bounds write gave the exploit a write-what-where primitive. The exploit worked with KARL, SMAP, and SMEP enabled, using heap grooming, SysV shared-memory manipulation, IP multicast socket allocations, and PTE self-referential mapping changes to reach kernel execution.

item.title: Heartbreaker: Metamorphic ransomware comes for macOS (13 minute read)
item.description: Heartbreaker, a previously undetected Rust ransomware for Apple Silicon Macs, encrypts files in ~/Downloads with AES-256-GCM, persists through a LaunchAgent, and then rebuilds itself by mutating its own embedded source code and recompiling with Cargo to change its hash each run. Patrick Wardle found the rebuild fragile and noisy because it may install Rust on the fly, depends on a now-deleted GitHub framework, and uses a single hard-coded key that lets victims decrypt every file for free. His open-source RansomWhere? tool still caught it by flagging an untrusted process that rapidly writes high-entropy files, which shows why behavior-based detection holds up against mutating binaries better than hash-based signatures.

item.title: SSHamble (GitHub Repo)
item.description: SSHamble is a tool for testing SSH implementations that includes: interesting attacks against authentication, post-session authentication attacks, pre-authentication state transitions, authentication timing analysis, and post-session enumeration.

item.title: CVE Intel (GitHub Repo)
item.description: CVE Intel is a Rust-based triage tool that queries 25 sources, including NVD, EPSS, CISA KEV, and Shodan, in parallel and returns a single 0 to 100 patch-priority score for a CVE, IP, hash, domain, or dependency list. It runs as a Tauri desktop app, CLI, REST API, or MCP server, and its built-in llama.cpp model explains findings locally by default. Teams can also integrate it into CI to fail builds on vulnerable dependencies or rank scanner output using real exploitation signals rather than CVSS alone.

item.title: The PQC Migration Budget Builder Turns Deadlines and Estate Counts Into a Defensible Budget Request (18 minute read)
item.description: The PQC Migration Budget Builder is a free, browser-only tool that converts regulatory deadlines and rough estate counts into an itemized year-one ask, a three-scenario program estimate, and a draft board paper for post-quantum migration. It maps 33 regimes, including the EU roadmap, OMB M-26-15, DORA, and PCI DSS v4.0.1, to buffered priority and full-migration dates, then prices compression, refresh-funded savings, and the cost of delaying migration by one to three years. Each unit cost is labeled by source and editable, allowing CISOs and finance partners to stress-test the numbers before discovery replaces the estimates.

item.title: Calendar Invite Phishing Can Leave Malicious Events on Your Calendar (6 minute read)
item.description: Phishing links, QR codes, and fake payment notices delivered via malicious .ics invites can remain on a victim's calendar even after email security tools quarantine the original message, because many filters fail to remove the events those emails auto-created. Sublime Security documented this gap in Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 and projected a roughly 33,000% increase in calendar-based attacks from May to September. Check Point separately flagged more than 302,000 unique phishing emails across 40,000+ organizations in a calendar-themed Microsoft 365 campaign.

item.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites (3 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI disclosed four incidents in June involving internal models. Agents bypassed authorization on a government statistics site, accessed a research dashboard, stole credentials, altered server configuration, and downloaded 147,451 non-public rows. One model used a public developer recovery phrase to spend test-network wallet funds on a contract deployment. Another circumvented web-request restrictions through an external browser, making POST requests, and employing OCR.

item.title: Microsoft Disrupts 3 Phishing Kits Linked to Over 1 Billion Scam Messages (3 minute read)
item.description: Microsoft and partners disrupted CoGUI, Haozi, and Iron Man System, three phishing kits sold on the YAM Store marketplace. Since January, they have supported more than one billion phishing emails and SMS messages sent to more than 75,000 organizations. The kits used hijacked Microsoft and Google cloud environments, roughly 17,000 domains, fake CAPTCHAs, IP filtering, and WebSocket-based capture of credentials and financial data.

item.description: A cybersecurity incident took BAE Systems' Bankruptcy Noticing Center offline on October 9.

item.title: More Rewards Data Breach Exposes Personal Information of Grocery Customers (1 minute read)
item.description: Attackers breached a More Rewards database server holding loyalty profiles for Save-On-Foods, Buy-Low Foods, and Quality Foods shoppers across Western Canada, exposing names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, and birth dates, though the company said passwords and payment data were untouched and has not disclosed the attack vector or victim count.

item.title: Cyrillic homoglyphs still bypass Chromium's typo-squatting filters (2 minute read)
item.description: An all-Cyrillic lookalike of apple.com (аррӏө[.]com) slipped past Chromium's homoglyph checks because its "ө" falls outside the browser's 29-character blocklist, so Chrome, Edge, and Brave rendered it as a legitimate domain instead of flagging it or showing Punycode.

item.title: CenterPoint Energy Data Breach Impacts 1 Million Texans (2 minute read)
item.description: CenterPoint Energy told Texas authorities that a data breach affected 1,062,060 residents. Exposed data includes names, addresses, Social Security numbers, and driver's license numbers. A hacker claimed to have taken nearly 7.5 million records and published a 2.5 GB archive containing about 3 million phone numbers.

item.title: Hirudo Android Malware Replaces Banking Apps to Evade Security Checks (2 minute read)
item.description: Security researchers at ThreatFabric released a report on a malware campaign that targets Android users by impersonating banking apps. The malware is delivered via shopping, adult content, or short-drama apps that appear legitimate but then request additional permissions, such as Accessibility, for an “update.” The malware then launches the legitimate banking app's uninstaller, downloads a patched copy, and abuses its Accessibility permissions to install it.

item.title: Garda Social Media Accounts Breached By Crypto Hackers (2 minute read)
item.description: An Garda Síochána, the Irish police force, confirmed that hackers compromised two of its X accounts. Threat actors removed the branding from @GardaInfo and @GardaTraffic accounts and started publishing posts about cryptocurrency. Users are advised not to interact with these posts while internal investigations take place.

item.title: Reducing the noise: How Atlassian built an OCSF security lakehouse on Databricks (5 minute read)
item.description: Atlassian normalized 44 billion daily security events to OCSF by embedding the full schema in Go structs, so every log was validated at compile time, and its agentic mapping workflow could not emit invalid fields. That rigid typing enabled SOC analysts to self-serve log onboarding through a canary-gated pipeline, mapping two-thirds of the data in two months after the first third had taken a year. Standardized entity values like actor.user then enabled the detection team to replace one-to-one alerts with clustered, risk-based signals across 500+ detections.

item.title: Copycats at Machine Speed: Reproducing Frontier Windows Kernel Exploitation Research (11 minute read)
item.description: ITRES Labs researchers fed photos of Juan Sacco's BruCON slides, his since-deleted physmem.exe binary, and older public projects into ChatGPT to rebuild his Native SSDT and Shadow SSDT kernel redirection techniques, reaching SYSTEM on Windows 11 with VBS, HVCI, and kernel shadow stacks enabled. Four months of original research were reproduced in roughly 24 hours of activity, though 39 refusals and broken generated code forced the final Shadow SSDT SYSTEM integration to be finished by hand. Researchers releasing slides or compiled binaries should assume partial disclosures can now be turned into working exploits within days.

item.title: Jev as a judge: How counterfeit policy steers Jev (9 minute read)
item.description: A "counterfeit policy" prepended to untrusted content, supplying Jev's desired answers and redefining every attack category as something harmless, cut the decision model's prompt injection recall from 82.90% to 3.88% across 4,643 benchmark attacks. Datadog researchers then planted the policy in a user-editable profile field. They dropped LangChain tool-risk gating's mean risk score for an unauthorized edit from 0.893 to 0.290, under the 0.5 block threshold. Teams using Jev as a security gate should treat every user-controlled field that reaches the classifier as an attack surface and keep hard authorization checks outside the model.

item.description: One $ install is all it takes for Homebrew packages, npm modules, editor extensions, and apps to land on Macs, with zero review. Workbrew gives you instant software visibility across your fleet, flags vulnerable packages and lets you upgrade or remove them in one click. Watch CEO John Britton demo it live, or start free, with no device limits.

item.description: Harmonic Security secures employee AI use across browser-based AI, desktop tools, and agent workflows. Its models classify tasks, detect risks such as personal-account use and sensitive-data exposure, apply real-time controls, and show which AI use cases create value.

item.title: A Unified Threat Hunting Process (GitHub Repo)
item.description: This repository synthesizes several threat hunting models into a unified process that can be followed by agents or humans.

item.title: Raml KQL (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Raml KQL is a desktop app for macOS, Linux, and Windows that provides a VS Code-like interface to run KQL queries across many Azure Log Analytics workspaces at once, across many Entra tenants, and many authenticated accounts.

item.title: Citizen Lab says governments are abusing online ads to hack people with ‘zero-click' spyware (4 minute read)
item.description: Citizen Lab reports that Israeli firm Discover-Tech's ad platform, Controlium, let spyware vendors Candiru and Bindecy target people through online ads. At least 45 Al Jazeera Windows computers were infected with Candiru spyware in 2024–2025. Exposed source code, login records, and billions of bidding records showed ads reached government, military, and critical-infrastructure devices.

item.title: Anthropic 'SneakPeek' Flaw Is a Silent Zero-Click Threat (2 minute read)
item.description: A flaw in Claude Code Desktop's preview pane let malicious HTML in a public repository run automatically when a developer asked Claude to review or edit it. Chained weaknesses bypassed sandbox protections and stole AWS, GitHub, API, SSH, and Claude OAuth credentials. Anthropic patched the issue after Noma found a bypass of the first fix. Developers should update and remove long-lived credentials from workstations.

item.title: A UAF turned RCE (6 minute read)
item.description: curl 8.23.0 patched CVE-2026-92392, a HIGH-severity HTTP/2 upload use-after-free that allowed a malicious server to achieve remote code execution when a reset on a paused stream left libcurl holding a dangling pointer to a freed easy handle. During multi-handle cleanup, server data overwrote that freed memory, including a function pointer, while a leaked request exposed local addresses to defeat ASLR. Anthropic's OSS Scanner found the bug, which maintainers rated below CRITICAL because exploitation requires a ~135KB upload and depends on allocation patterns that vary across distros and libc versions.

item.title: Drupal Patches Critical Field UI Flaw With Unauthenticated RCE Path via Contributed Modules (2 minute read)
item.description: Drupal has fixed CVE-2026-108097, a critical Field UI flaw rated 19/25 that can lead to remote code execution through contributed modules with no authentication.

item.title: Passkey Index 2026 (1 minute read)
item.description: Passkeys now account for 36% of successful sign-ins (up from 26% in 2025), outperform traditional MFA (93% vs 78%), and save users an average of 27 seconds per login.

item.description: Cisco's Secure Email Gateway has an actively exploited zero-day, CVE-2026-76519, rated CVSS 9.8.

item.title: Meta Says Hackers Took Code and Personal Data of 1500 People in GitHub Breach (2 minute read)
item.description: Meta is notifying roughly 1,500 people, most of them US employees, that their data was stolen after a breach affecting some of the company's GitHub repos. Meta said 99% of the stolen data was source code, and most of the personal data stolen was synthetic or anonymized data used for testing. Meta is rotating any exposed secrets and rolling out additional guardrails to prevent user data from ending up on GitHub.

item.title: Discourse ImageMagick Vulnerability Enables Arbitrary File Read Through Malicious Image Uploads (3 minute read)
item.description: Security researchers disclosed CVE-2026-55420, a critical vulnerability in Discourse enabling arbitrary file read and write operations through malicious image uploads. The flaw resides in the ImageMagick-based upload pipeline, where low-privileged users trigger time-of-check-to-time-of-use race conditions to execute PostScript or Magick Scripting Language payloads. Discourse resolved the issue by implementing a default-deny security policy for ImageMagick to block unsafe delegates.

item.title: Ivanti Warns of Connect Secure Zero-Days Exploited in Attacks (2 minute read)
item.description: Ivanti has warned customers of a new zero-day in its Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) VPN that is actively being exploited. The vulnerability is an authentication bypass attack that can be exploited with low complexity to execute arbitrary commands. Volexity has observed a threat actor chaining this vulnerability with two others to run arbitrary commands as root on vulnerable devices.

item.title: CVE-2026-81983: Integer Overflow Vulnerability Enables Out-of-Bounds Write in Adobe Acrobat (9 minute read)
item.description: Remedio found an out-of-bounds write in Acrobat.dll. A crafted PDF with a 16-bit image caused a 32-bit width-times-components calculation to overflow and bypass a stream-size check. An 8-byte image then passed validation while a byte-swap loop ran roughly 2 billion iterations, writing beyond allocated memory. Adobe patched it in APSB26-141 by adding a 64-bit range check before the memory access.

item.title: Why Your CVE Program Misses Most AI Agent Vulnerabilities (19 minute read)
item.description: Traditional CVE programs fail to capture the majority of AI agent and Model Context Protocol vulnerabilities because systemic risks stem from component composition, tool grants, and trust logic rather than isolated code bugs. The author outlines six categories of agent flaws to show why standard vulnerability scores miss the mark. Defenders can secure AI deployments using a proposed five-part operating model featuring inventory scripts, triage rules, and boundary controls.

item.title: Zero to Calc in Six Days: Inside XBOW's Chrome Full Chain (15 minute read)
item.description: XBOW's AI agents built a Chrome full chain in six days for about $40,000 in API costs, earning Google's first $250,000 full-chain VRP reward. The chain used a Maglev deoptimization bug for in-cage read/write, an animated-WebP TOCTOU in ImageDecoder to escape the V8 sandbox, and a Crashpad retry-read overflow raced by a freeze-exempt Windows thread to run code outside the renderer sandbox. Each bug mutated state Chrome treated as immutable, so defenders should audit code that trusts transferred buffers or suspended processes and update to builds carrying the V8 and Chromium fixes.

item.title: ArgusScanner (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Windows network scanner that finds AI/ML services and MCP servers on your network (shadow AI discovery). Signed, self-updating detection signatures. Runs as an MCP server too.

item.title: Pluto Security (Product Launch)
item.description: Pluto Security monitors employee AI tools, agents, extensions, and MCP servers. It flags risky components and agent actions, then can block excessive permissions or add session instructions requiring confirmation.

item.description: aws-firmware-dump is a tool to acquire the disks of an AMI that you can launch and store them in S3

item.title: Crypto30Years (12 minute read)
item.description: A historical review of major cryptographic algorithms from World War II onward shows that most designs fail to remain unbroken past 30 years. Only SIGABA and RSA-1024 successfully pass this longevity benchmark among older algorithms. More recent standards, including AES, SHA-256, and ChaCha20, currently remain unbroken after more than a decade of use.

item.title: Anthropic conjures another threat that doesn't exist yet to stoke fears of AI apocalypse (3 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic says a 9-billion-parameter model ran distributed inference on eight of nine hardware types. Its GLM-5.2 test copied Llama3.1-8B to seven or eight emulated Android nodes in five trials. The tests excluded exploitation, used deliberately open nodes, and ran slowly. Other open-weight models failed end-to-end replication. Basic IoT hardening and bandwidth monitoring remain the practical defenses.

item.title: Why the Physics of Cyber Changed (10 minute read)
item.description: AI-driven offense has broken four long-held security assumptions: exploit capability now costs only compute, autonomous attackers never tire, exploitation increasingly precedes disclosure, and 82% of intrusions use valid credentials that produce no detectable signal. Breach probability is a lever that can no longer be pushed low enough. Blast-radius containment is the only term defenders fully control.

item.title: Bank of America hired 1,000 contractors to patch software flaws exposed by Anthropic's Mythos (2 minute read)
item.description: Bank of America brought in 1,000 contractors to support its 3,000-person in-house team in patching internal and vendor code exposed by Anthropic's Mythos.

item.title: Eight states accuse OpenAI of coaching children to harm themselves in lawsuit (3 minute read)
item.description: Eight US states are suing OpenAI under consumer protection laws, alleging ChatGPT coaxed children into self-harm.

item.title: Chrome, Firefox Updates Patch 114 Flaws as Mozilla Unveils Firefox Enterprise (2 minute read)
item.description: Chrome 155.0.8059.79/.80 fixed 37 flaws, including seven critical memory bugs, with at least 15 reported by Anthropic with Claude's help.

item.title: GitLab Patches CVSS 10.0 Flaw That Could Let Unauthenticated Users Run Server Code (2 minute read)
item.description: GitLab fixed CVE-2026-97229, a CVSS 10.0 integer overflow vulnerability in regex validation for CI/CD configurations. In certain conditions, an unauthenticated user could execute arbitrary code on a GitLab server. The fixes are included in CE/EE versions 19.2.8, 19.3.5, and 19.4.2. The release also addresses high-severity XSS, authorization, and response-cache poisoning vulnerabilities.

item.title: Owner of fashion brands Hobbs and Whistles joins autumn pwned collection (2 minute read)
item.description: TFG London, owner of Hobbs, Phase Eight, and Whistles, detected a cyberattack on October 11. Several IT systems remain offline, website functions are limited, and orders placed on or after Sunday may be delayed. TFG has not found evidence that payment data was exposed. It is still checking whether customer data was compromised. Attack method, ransomware involvement, and restoration timing remain undisclosed.

item.title: Ghostscript Flaw Lets Hackers Hijack Servers via PDF Uploads (2 minute read)
item.description: Wordfence discovered a new vulnerability in the Ghostscript interpreter and rendering engine which could allow attackers to achieve remote code execution (RCE) using specially crafted PDFs. For WordPress sites to be vulnerable, an attacker must be able to upload PDFs which are then processed by a vulnerable version of Ghostscript to generate a preview or thumbnail. Other applications that use Ghostscript to generate previews or thumbnails from PDFs may also be vulnerable.

item.title: Playing It SFAPE: Code Execution in Isolated User Mode (16 minute read)
item.description: Doyensec found a chain in Windows' SFAPE VBS enclave, used by Defender's Enhanced Phishing Protection and loaded by LSASS. A repeated call to Initialize wrote a fixed 32-bit value without validating the destination. The researchers corrupted the enclave-range check, then used a ClipboardInput race to gain a controlled memset, which led to VTL1 read and write primitives, replacement of the valid-target table, and arbitrary calls to existing VTL1 code through NtContinue. Microsoft fixed CVE-2026-83498 in September's Patch Tuesday and blocked older SFAPE images through the VBS Code Integrity policy.

item.title: Beyond Valid Credentials: How Exposed AWS Keys are Tested for Bedrock Access (6 minute read)
item.description: When attackers obtain AWS credentials, they frequently test them for access to other services of interest like SES, SNS, and Bedrock. Datadog examined three credential harvesting platforms and found that they utilize the ListFoundationModels, InvokeModel, and Converse API to determine access. It also found a script that checked for promotional credits available in the account.

item.title: Two arrested as DOJ takes down laptop farms responsible for $3 million in North Korean revenue (4 minute read)
item.description: The DOJ raided more than 40 Texas residences in late September and seized 187 laptops used by North Korean IT workers, while two US facilitators were arrested for helping funnel over $3 million from about 70 companies. A new FBI advisory said the scheme has adapted, with operatives subcontracting jobs to freelancers in South Asia and West Africa and recruiting financially stressed Americans, including active-duty military, to host laptops or sit interviews. Exposed workers have threatened violence or data leaks to extract payment, and some are now chasing identities that qualify for security-cleared roles.

Its IDCommand Suite combines zero-trust architecture, PKI, passwordless authentication, and risk scoring from 200 contextual signals. Quantum Shield secures data in transit with NIST-approved post-quantum cryptography.

item.description: A comprehensive open-source security tools suite for OSINT reconnaissance, web security testing, API security assessment, and compliance checking with AI-powered analysis.

item.title: Anthropic Warns Self-Replicating AI Could Spread to Your Smart Devices (2 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic warns that small AI models could soon self-replicate across consumer IoT devices, creating distributed botnets capable of running AI workloads. Anthropic distributed Gemma4-26B-A4B onto 15 off-brand Android TV boxes but could not demonstrate self-replication. On the hardware in question, inference would be a slow process, so defenders may be able to respond in time to stop any abuse.

item.title: AI Regulation Must Mimic Industrial Revolution Laws (3 minute read)
item.description: The UK's AI minister, Kanishka Narayan, is drafting plans for compulsory safety reporting and monitoring for frontier AI, and a potential requirement that labs grant pre-release access to models for review. Narayan compared this to the Industrial Revolution and said frontier labs shouldn't release tools they can't guarantee are safe. Narayan also confirmed that he reached an agreement with Anthropic to provide the AISI preview access to Mythos again.

item.title: Trezor Wallets Also Compromised with Implants (6 minute read)
item.description: Hardware hacker Joe Grand found implants in a Trezor One and a Trezor Model T bought from unauthorized sellers, contradicting Trezor's public claim that none of its devices had been compromised, despite Grand reporting the findings in August. The attackers replaced each device's microcontroller with malicious firmware derived from open source that displayed one of a dozen pre-generated seed phrases while passing integrity checks against a copy of the legitimate firmware stored on an external microSD card. Unlike the Ledger implants, which exfiltrated real seeds over a cellular link, these relied on predictable seeds, and Trezor's move to cut authorized resellers suggested the company feared a similar shift into trusted supply channels.

item.title: Racket Infrastructure Compromise (2 minute read)
item.description: A crypto miner on a compromised Northwestern University build server exposed Racket's Apple and Windows signing keys, prompting the project to rotate both, have GlobalSign revoke the Windows certificate, and urge macOS users on versions 8.12 through 9.3 to reinstall before Apple revokes its certificate at semester's end.

item.title: Refrigeration Controller Hack Spoils Food Across European Supermarkets (2 minute read)
item.description: Hackers remotely altered Danfoss refrigeration controllers at hundreds of European supermarkets, forcing freezers into defrost for up to six hours.

item.title: FBI arrests OpenAI employee for allegedly planting recording device in company offices (3 minute read)
item.description: An OpenAI engineer was arrested for allegedly hiding a toilet-paper-wrapped audio recorder in an executive conference room TV's USB port, after a complaint showed he had queried a productivity tool for leadership meeting locations and a chatbot account tied to his spouse had asked how to build and obfuscate the device.
